@{5c096c483ce7d43ae0f1177e|full_name}: At this point I'm pretty sure this is a case of you distorting the truth. He likely got banned because the avatars *were* in fact public cancer, because of his behavior, or because he was using alternate avatars at the same time that WERE cancer.

If the avatar itself was public use and he got banned for it, you likely would have gotten banned as well. That should say enough about what you are considered to be by the public eye. This is further extended by the amount of screen shaders and extreme particle effects you release on VRCMods alone. 

Slapping on a tag to allow CLEARLY obnoxious, annoying, cancerous and generally TOS-breaking effects and sounds on an avatar should not be considered. Keep that stuff to a private instance out of anybody's way. Just like you would with R-18 avatars.

Being a creator, I'm all for giving rights and customizability to all content creators. But this... This is not the way to go about it. 
This only supports you, your friends, and people very similar to you. Not content creators as a whole.

Giving people the freedom to create content is important. However, making (and distributing) malicious avatars isn't OK. If you choose to make things designed to be unpleasant, you're likely to run into issues with players as well as moderation.

Additionally, no matter what content you choose to upload to VRChat, you must abide by the Community Guidelines and Terms of Service. Roughly speaking, the Community Guidelines prohibits content that can be used to harass or "troll" other users. No matter the original intent or use case of the content in question, if an avatar (for example) is considered harassing, malicious, or abusive, it can and will be removed from the service at the discretion of the VRChat Moderation team.

We ask that you use common sense in determining what could be used in this manner. The Safety System is meant as a mitigation for users abusing avatar systems, and is not an excuse for avatar creators to create abuse-able setups or systems.

As a final addendum, no matter the checkboxes available in the SDK, content must never violate the Community Guidelines or Terms of Service.

Hello to all my name is Neko: 3 I ask you to read this and share it with everyone.

I want to make sure that the vrchat avatar creators get more rights. Since some of my friends have been banned for their avatars (public animation avatars), I request another option in the vrchat sdk (button annoying avatar or something similar) as there are such features there are also avatars for gore and 18+. This option in the SDK should be an important part of the Safty Settings (annoying avatars on / off in each category)

More info About The annoying avatar button

-When akiv, players can decide in the Safty settings themselves if they want to see avatars with such animations.

-When do I know when to use the button?

Once the avatar has a loud audio (boosted volume or range).
Once full screen shader is used on an avatar (screen shake or fractal shader etc.).
-By too many particles are active (particle spam).

Such avatars should nevertheless be put on public worlds!
With the Safty Settings anyone can decide whether he wants to see such avatars or not !!

Added this And stop deleting such avatars and ban the creator! If you add this option and people upload such avatars without the option, it is ok to distribute a warning / ban.

But it can not stay the way it is at the moment !! So I ask the Vrchat devs to be more gracious in their content creator.
title: More Rights for the Content Creators
